MERIDIAN CAPITAL PARTNERS
FULL PORTFOLIO AND GOVERNANCE REPORT
Fiscal Years 2023–2025 | Prepared by: Investment Committee Secretariat
Date: March 31, 2025
STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL — FOR AUTHORISED RECIPIENTS ONLY

==============================================================================
PART 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
==============================================================================

Meridian Capital Partners closed Fiscal Year 2024 with $6.8 billion in assets under management across eight active funds spanning growth equity, infrastructure, climate transition, credit opportunities, and special situations strategies.

The firm's flagship Meridian Growth Fund IV delivered a net IRR of 19.2% through December 31, 2024, outperforming the Cambridge Associates Global Venture benchmark of 14.1% by 510 basis points.  Robert Ashworth, Managing Partner, attributed the outperformance to concentrated positions in high-conviction software and healthcare technology companies.

Meridian Infrastructure Fund II delivered a net IRR of 11.8%, in line with the firm's underwriting assumptions.  Kweku Mensah, General Partner leading the infrastructure practice, noted that rising interest rates created headwinds in the second half of 2024 but that the portfolio's contracted cash flows provided resilience.

Meridian Climate Opportunities Fund I achieved a net IRR of 14.7% in its third year, driven primarily by the unrealised appreciation in CarbonBridge and TerraFund.  Sophie Leclercq, Head of ESG and Impact Measurement, highlighted that the fund's carbon avoidance metrics exceeded the target by 23%.

The Investment Committee, chaired by Robert Ashworth and comprising fifteen senior professionals, convened twelve times during fiscal 2024 and ratified fifteen formal investment decisions.  Full minutes are reproduced in Part 5 of this report.

Alejandro Torres, CFO, reported that the firm's cost-to-income ratio improved to 48.3% from 51.7% in the prior year, reflecting operational leverage as AUM grew by $1.4 billion.  Fee-related earnings increased to $112M, representing an 18% increase year-on-year.

Tomasz Kowalczyk, Chief Risk Officer, conducted a comprehensive portfolio risk review in Q4 2024.  The review identified three companies — DataForge, ZephyrData, and VaultChain — as requiring elevated monitoring due to balance-sheet stress and deteriorating unit economics.  Appropriate reserves and valuation adjustments have been recorded.

Priscilla Fontaine, General Partner for Growth Equity, led the firm's largest single investment in fiscal 2024: the $45M participation in NovaPay's Series C round at a $220M pre-money valuation.  NovaPay's annualised payment volume reached $2.3B by year-end, a 340% increase from the prior year.

Diana Ostrowski, Partner covering Consumer and Healthcare, oversaw QuantumHealth's acquisition of CoastalMed, creating a vertically integrated digital-health platform with over 1.2 million active patients.  The combined entity is on track for a 2026 IPO.

Ingrid Nystrom joined the Investment Committee as Partner, Technology Sector, replacing Yuki Tanaka who was promoted to Managing Director with a focus on Asia-Pacific expansion.  Marcus Delacroix was promoted from Principal to Partner in the Infrastructure practice, effective January 2025.

------------------------------------------------------------
Governance Framework
------------------------------------------------------------

The Investment Committee operates under a formal governance framework adopted in 2019 and most recently updated in January 2024.  All investment decisions above $5M require a quorum of at least seven members, with approval by a simple majority of those present.

Decisions above $50M require supermajority approval (ten of sixteen members) and a mandatory 48-hour deliberation period following the initial presentation.  Robert Ashworth, as Chair, holds a casting vote in the event of a tie.

James Whitfield, General Counsel, maintains the decisions register and ensures that all resolutions are consistent with the constitutional documents of each fund.  Tomasz Kowalczyk provides a risk assessment memorandum for every investment above $10M.

The Investment Committee adopted a revised conflicts-of-interest policy in March 2024, requiring disclosure of any direct or indirect financial interest held by a committee member in a target company or its competitors.  Helena Voss recused herself from the ZephyrData bridge financing discussion under this policy.

ESG screening, led by Sophie Leclercq, is mandatory for all new investments.  The firm's responsible investment policy prohibits investments in companies deriving more than 15% of revenue from thermal coal, tobacco, or controversial weapons.

Yuki Tanaka chairs the fund's Advisory Committee, which met three times during 2024 to review performance and approve valuation methodologies.

The fund's investment period closed on December 31, 2024.  The team is focused on value creation at the existing portfolio rather than new origination.

PART 4: PORTFOLIO COMPANY DEEP DIVES
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
QuantumHealth
------------------------------------------------------------

Sector:                FinTech
Stage at Entry:        Series B
Cost Basis:            $15M
Current Fair Value:    $22M
Unrealised Gain/Loss:  $7M
Meridian Board Seat:   Robert Ashworth
Board Observer:        Kweku Mensah

QuantumHealth was founded in 2016 and has grown to become a leading fintech platform serving enterprise clients across North America and Europe.  The company employs 80 full-time staff and operates from offices in London, New York, and Singapore.

Meridian first invested in QuantumHealth at the Series B round.  Robert Ashworth led the investment committee presentation and was appointed to the board following close.  The original investment thesis centred on the company's differentiated technology and a large, underpenetrated addressable market.

Revenue for fiscal 2024 grew 60% year-on-year to $8M ARR.  Gross margin expanded from 55% to 62% as the company scaled its infrastructure and reduced hosting costs through a cloud-cost optimisation programme.

The company raised a $30M Series B round in Q1 2024, led by a prominent global technology investor, with Meridian participating pro-rata.  Post-round, Meridian's ownership stands at 12.0% on a fully diluted basis.

Customer concentration remains the company's primary strategic risk.  Kweku Mensah and the management team have implemented a comprehensive mitigation plan, including diversifying the customer base.  Tomasz Kowalczyk has reviewed and approved the risk mitigation framework.

The company's management team, led by CEO Alexandra Brandt, has consistently delivered against its quarterly milestones.  The board met six times in fiscal 2024 and approved a revised three-year strategic plan targeting $40M ARR by 2027.

==============================================================================
PART 5: INVESTMENT COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Investment Committee Meeting — Q1 2021
------------------------------------------------------------

Date:        January 16, 2021
Chair:       Robert Ashworth
Secretary:   James Whitfield
Present:     Robert Ashworth, Priscilla Fontaine, Kweku Mensah, Yuki Tanaka, Diana Ostrowski, Alejandro Torres, Sophie Leclercq, Tomasz Kowalczyk, Helena Voss, Marcus Delacroix, Ingrid Nystrom
Apologies:   Basil Okonkwo, Camille Renard

1. OPENING AND QUORUM

Robert Ashworth opened the meeting at 09:00 and confirmed that a quorum of 11 members was present, satisfying the constitutional requirement for binding resolutions.

2. MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETING

The minutes of the meeting held in October 2020 were reviewed and approved without amendment.  James Whitfield confirmed that all action items had been completed.

3. PORTFOLIO REVIEW

Sophie Leclercq presented an update on TerraFund.  Revenue for the trailing twelve months was $15M, representing 50% growth year-on-year.  Sophie Leclercq confirmed that the company is tracking ahead of plan and remains on course for the milestones outlined in the most recent board paper.

Tomasz Kowalczyk presented an update on PinnacleOps.  Revenue for the trailing twelve months was $30M, representing 70% growth year-on-year.  Tomasz Kowalczyk confirmed that the company is tracking ahead of plan and remains on course for the milestones outlined in the most recent board paper.

Helena Voss presented an update on ZephyrData.  Revenue for the trailing twelve months was $45M, representing 90% growth year-on-year.  Helena Voss confirmed that the company is tracking ahead of plan and remains on course for the milestones outlined in the most recent board paper.

4. NEW INVESTMENT PROPOSALS

Tomasz Kowalczyk presented an investment memorandum for CoastalMed, proposing a $18M commitment at a $90M pre-money valuation.  The committee discussed the opportunity at length, focusing on the competitive landscape, management team quality, and exit pathway.  Following deliberation, the committee approved the investment subject to satisfactory completion of legal due diligence and reference checks.

Helena Voss presented an investment memorandum for Luminara, proposing a $33M commitment at a $165M pre-money valuation.  The committee discussed the opportunity at length, focusing on the competitive landscape, management team quality, and exit pathway.  Following deliberation, the committee approved the investment subject to satisfactory completion of legal due diligence and reference checks.

5. RISK ITEMS

Tomasz Kowalczyk presented the quarterly risk report.  Luminara was flagged as requiring elevated monitoring following a miss on Q1 revenue targets.  The committee instructed the lead partner to arrange a call with the CEO within ten business days and to report back at the next meeting.

6. ANY OTHER BUSINESS

James Whitfield raised a housekeeping matter regarding LP reporting timelines.  It was agreed that the next LP update letter would be issued by the 15th of the following month.

7. DATE OF NEXT MEETING

The next meeting of the Investment Committee will be held in April 2021.  James Whitfield to circulate the agenda no fewer than five business days in advance.

Meeting closed at 17:30.

Signed: Robert Ashworth (Chair)
Countersigned: James Whitfield (Secretary)

Basil Okonkwo presented an update on PulseGrid.  Revenue for the trailing twelve months was $45M, representing 90% growth year-on-year.  Basil Okonkwo confirmed that the company is tracking ahead of plan and remains on course for the milestones outlined in the most recent board paper.

4. NEW INVESTMENT PROPOSALS

Ingrid Nystrom presented an investment memorandum for MeridianAI, proposing a $18M commitment at a $90M pre-money valuation.  The committee discussed the opportunity at length, focusing on the competitive landscape, management team quality, and exit pathway.  Following deliberation, the committee approved the investment subject to satisfactory completion of legal due diligence and reference checks.

Basil Okonkwo presented an investment memorandum for BioNexus, proposing a $33M commitment at a $165M pre-money valuation.  The committee discussed the opportunity at length, focusing on the competitive landscape, management team quality, and exit pathway.  Following deliberation, the committee approved the investment subject to satisfactory completion of legal due diligence and reference checks.

6. ANY OTHER BUSINESS

James Whitfield raised a housekeeping matter regarding LP reporting timelines.  It was agreed that the next LP update letter would be issued by the 15th of the following month.

Formal Investment Decisions — FY2024 and FY2025 YTD
------------------------------------------------------------

  DECISION ID        DATE         VOTE          DESCRIPTION
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ADR-2024-001       Jan 14, 2024 16-0          Approve continuation of NovaPay Series C investment at $45M
  ADR-2024-002       Feb 20, 2024 15-1          Authorize CarbonBridge follow-on at reduced valuation with protective provisions
  ADR-2024-003       Mar 18, 2024 14-2          Approve QuantumHealth acquisition of CoastalMed for $120M
  ADR-2024-004       Apr 22, 2024 13-3          Authorize write-down of DataForge position by 40% to reflect market conditions
  ADR-2024-005       May 13, 2024 12-4          Approve Meridian Growth Fund V first close at $800M
  ADR-2024-006       Jun 17, 2024 11-5          Authorize SkyLogistics IPO readiness assessment and banker selection
  ADR-2024-007       Jul 15, 2024 10-6          Approve MeridianAI Series A lead at $18M pre-money valuation
  ADR-2024-008       Aug 19, 2024 16-0          Ratify ESG scoring framework update to align with SFDR Article 9
  ADR-2024-009       Sep 16, 2024 15-1          Authorize IronBridge Infrastructure co-investment alongside Brookfield
  ADR-2024-010       Oct 14, 2024 14-2          Approve ZephyrData bridge financing at 20% discount to Series B
  ADR-2025-001       Nov 18, 2024 13-3          Approve VaultChain token economics restructuring and equity conversion
  ADR-2025-002       Dec 09, 2024 12-4          Authorize Luminara secondary sale to HarbourLane Capital at 2.1x cost
  ADR-2025-003       Jan 20, 2025 11-5          Approve FractalRobotics Series B participation at $60M valuation
  ADR-2025-004       Feb 17, 2025 10-6          Ratify revised LP reporting standards effective Q1 2025
  ADR-2025-005       Mar 10, 2025 16-0          Authorize TerraFund land acquisition programme Phase II


------------------------------------------------------------
Decision Narratives
------------------------------------------------------------

ADR-2024-001 — Approve continuation of NovaPay Series C investment at $45M

Proposed by: Robert Ashworth.  Seconded by: Yuki Tanaka.

Background: The Investment Committee reviewed a detailed memorandum prepared by Robert Ashworth covering the strategic rationale, financial projections, due diligence findings, and risk assessment for this resolution.  The committee noted the strong alignment with the fund's investment mandate and the attractive risk/return profile of the proposed action.

Discussion: Priscilla Fontaine noted the potential downside scenario and requested that Kweku Mensah prepare a sensitivity analysis for distribution within 48 hours.  James Whitfield confirmed that all legal conditions precedent had been satisfied.

Resolution: Approved by vote of 16-0.

ADR-2024-002 — Authorize CarbonBridge follow-on at reduced valuation with protective provisions

Proposed by: Priscilla Fontaine.  Seconded by: Diana Ostrowski.

Background: The Investment Committee reviewed a detailed memorandum prepared by Priscilla Fontaine covering the strategic rationale, financial projections, due diligence findings, and risk assessment for this resolution.  The committee noted the strong alignment with the fund's investment mandate and the attractive risk/return profile of the proposed action.

Discussion: Kweku Mensah noted the potential downside scenario and requested that Yuki Tanaka prepare a sensitivity analysis for distribution within 48 hours.  James Whitfield confirmed that all legal conditions precedent had been satisfied.

Resolution: Approved by vote of 15-1.

ADR-2024-003 — Approve QuantumHealth acquisition of CoastalMed for $120M

Proposed by: Kweku Mensah.  Seconded by: Alejandro Torres.

Background: The Investment Committee reviewed a detailed memorandum prepared by Kweku Mensah covering the strategic rationale, financial projections, due diligence findings, and risk assessment for this resolution.  The committee noted the strong alignment with the fund's investment mandate and the attractive risk/return profile of the proposed action.

Discussion: Yuki Tanaka noted the potential downside scenario and requested that Diana Ostrowski prepare a sensitivity analysis for distribution within 48 hours.  James Whitfield confirmed that all legal conditions precedent had been satisfied.

Resolution: Approved by vote of 14-2.

ADR-2024-004 — Authorize write-down of DataForge position by 40% to reflect market conditions

Proposed by: Yuki Tanaka.  Seconded by: Sophie Leclercq.

Background: The Investment Committee reviewed a detailed memorandum prepared by Yuki Tanaka covering the strategic rationale, financial projections, due diligence findings, and risk assessment for this resolution.  The committee noted the strong alignment with the fund's investment mandate and the attractive risk/return profile of the proposed action.

Discussion: Diana Ostrowski noted the potential downside scenario and requested that Alejandro Torres prepare a sensitivity analysis for distribution within 48 hours.  James Whitfield confirmed that all legal conditions precedent had been satisfied.

Resolution: Approved by vote of 13-3.

ADR-2024-008 — Ratify ESG scoring framework update to align with SFDR Article 9

Proposed by: Tomasz Kowalczyk.  Seconded by: Ingrid Nystrom.

Background: The Investment Committee reviewed a detailed memorandum prepared by Tomasz Kowalczyk covering the strategic rationale, financial projections, due diligence findings, and risk assessment for this resolution.  The committee noted the strong alignment with the fund's investment mandate and the attractive risk/return profile of the proposed action.

Discussion: Helena Voss noted the potential downside scenario and requested that Marcus Delacroix prepare a sensitivity analysis for distribution within 48 hours.  James Whitfield confirmed that all legal conditions precedent had been satisfied.

Resolution: Approved by vote of 16-0.

==============================================================================
PART 7: ESG AND IMPACT MEASUREMENT
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
ESG Framework and Policy
------------------------------------------------------------

Meridian Capital Partners is a signatory to the United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment (UNPRI) and the Net Zero Asset Managers initiative.  The firm's ESG policy, maintained by Sophie Leclercq, was last comprehensively updated in Q1 2024 to align with the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) Article 9 requirements for the Climate Opportunities funds.

All new investments are subject to a pre-investment ESG screening, which scores each target company across four dimensions: Environmental Impact, Social Responsibility, Governance Quality, and Stakeholder Alignment.  Companies scoring below 60 out of 100 on the composite index are subject to enhanced due diligence and may not be approved without a remediation plan.

Sophie Leclercq chairs the ESG Committee, which comprises herself, Kweku Mensah, Diana Ostrowski, and an independent ESG advisor.  The committee meets quarterly and reviews portfolio-level ESG performance against the firm's impact thesis.

The firm's carbon footprint measurement programme, launched in 2022, now covers 89% of the portfolio by fair value.  Aggregate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions across the portfolio declined by 12% in fiscal 2024, ahead of the 8% annual reduction target.

Meridian's engagement policy requires lead partners to raise ESG-related matters at a minimum of two board meetings per year for each portfolio company.  Priscilla Fontaine reported that NovaPay achieved carbon neutrality for its Scope 1 and 2 emissions in Q3 2024, making it the first company in the growth equity portfolio to do so.

------------------------------------------------------------

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------

==============================================================================
PART 8: RISK REGISTER AND MITIGATION FRAMEWORK
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Risk Management Framework
------------------------------------------------------------

The firm's enterprise risk management framework, overseen by Tomasz Kowalczyk, classifies risks across five categories: Market Risk, Liquidity Risk, Operational Risk, Regulatory Risk, and Reputational Risk.  Each portfolio company is assigned a risk rating (1–5) that is reviewed quarterly.

Tomasz Kowalczyk presented the annual risk review to the Investment Committee on November 18, 2024.  The review highlighted three companies on the elevated-monitoring list and two macro-level risks (rising interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty in Eastern European markets) classified as Level 4 — High.

==============================================================================
PART 9: LP RELATIONS AND CAPITAL ACTIVITY
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
LP Base Overview
------------------------------------------------------------

Meridian's LP base comprises 94 distinct limited partners across seven categories.

  Sovereign Wealth Funds             12%
  Public Pension Funds               10%
  Insurance Companies                9%
  Endowments and Foundations         16%
  Family Offices                     22%
  Fund of Funds                      21%
  Corporate Investors                9%


------------------------------------------------------------
Capital Activity — FY2024
------------------------------------------------------------

Alejandro Torres presented the capital activity summary to the Investment Committee at the December 2024 meeting.  Total capital called during fiscal 2024 was $680M across six funds.  Total capital distributed was $420M, including the proceeds from four full exits and two secondary sales.

The firm's largest distribution in 2024 was the $180M return of capital and profit following the sale of ArborTech to a strategic acquirer at 3.8x MOIC.  Robert Ashworth described the exit as 'a textbook example of the firm's patient capital approach'.


==============================================================================
PART 10: STRATEGIC OUTLOOK 2025-2027
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Strategic Priorities 2025–2027
------------------------------------------------------------

1. Close Meridian Growth Fund V at target size of $1.2 billion, with a first close targeted for Q3 2025.  Priscilla Fontaine is leading LP outreach alongside Robert Ashworth.

2. Launch Meridian Infrastructure Fund III with a $900M target, incorporating a dedicated digital infrastructure sleeve.  Kweku Mensah and Marcus Delacroix will co-lead the fund.

3. Establish an Asia-Pacific office in Singapore, led by Yuki Tanaka, to originate and execute investments in high-growth technology companies across Southeast Asia, Japan, and South Korea.

4. Complete the rollout of the firm's proprietary portfolio management platform, MemOS, which will centralise company data, board materials, KPI tracking, and LP reporting.  Ingrid Nystrom is overseeing the technology implementation.

5. Achieve SFDR Article 9 classification for Meridian Climate Opportunities Fund II, targeted for launch in Q1 2026.  Sophie Leclercq is leading the product design and regulatory engagement.

6. Expand the firm's credit capabilities through a strategic hire of a dedicated credit partner.  Helena Voss is managing the search process with two short-listed candidates.

7. Implement a comprehensive diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) programme, including targets for investment team composition.  Fatima Al-Rashid and Diana Ostrowski are co-chairing the DEI working group.

QuantumHealth Board Meeting — March 2022
------------------------------------------------------------

Date:       March 10, 2022
Chair:      Yuki Tanaka
Attendees:  Yuki Tanaka, Diana Ostrowski, Alejandro Torres, Sophie Leclercq

Yuki Tanaka opened the board meeting and confirmed that the company had achieved $8M in annualised recurring revenue at the end of Q1 2022, representing 35% growth year-on-year.  CEO Carlos Mendez presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 62%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 18 months at the current burn rate.  Yuki Tanaka noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q3 2023 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 5 new engineering roles and 3 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Diana Ostrowski, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in June 2022.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Yuki Tanaka to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the June 2022 meeting.

Diana Ostrowski noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q4 2024 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 7 new engineering roles and 4 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Alejandro Torres, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in September 2023.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Diana Ostrowski to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the September 2023 meeting.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 68%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 27 months at the current burn rate.  Yuki Tanaka noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q2 2024 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 11 new engineering roles and 6 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Diana Ostrowski, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in March 2023.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Yuki Tanaka to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the March 2023 meeting.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 64%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 21 months at the current burn rate.  Yuki Tanaka noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q4 2025 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 7 new engineering roles and 4 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Diana Ostrowski, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in September 2024.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Yuki Tanaka to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the September 2024 meeting.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 68%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 27 months at the current burn rate.  Alejandro Torres noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q2 2025 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 11 new engineering roles and 6 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Sophie Leclercq, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in March 2024.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Alejandro Torres to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the March 2024 meeting.

Sophie Leclercq opened the board meeting and confirmed that the company had achieved $12M in annualised recurring revenue at the end of Q2 2022, representing 45% growth year-on-year.  CEO Alexandra Brandt presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 64%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 21 months at the current burn rate.  Sophie Leclercq noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q4 2023 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 7 new engineering roles and 4 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Tomasz Kowalczyk, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in September 2022.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Sophie Leclercq to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the September 2022 meeting.

Basil Okonkwo noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q1 2023 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 9 new engineering roles and 5 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Camille Renard, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in December 2022.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Basil Okonkwo to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the December 2022 meeting.

James Whitfield opened the board meeting and confirmed that the company had achieved $9M in annualised recurring revenue at the end of Q1 2023, representing 50% growth year-on-year.  CEO Alexandra Brandt presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 62%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 18 months at the current burn rate.  James Whitfield noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q3 2024 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 5 new engineering roles and 3 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Robert Ashworth, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in June 2023.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, James Whitfield to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the June 2023 meeting.

CEO Nadia Petrov presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 66%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 24 months at the current burn rate.  Priscilla Fontaine noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q1 2024 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 9 new engineering roles and 5 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Kweku Mensah, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in December 2023.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Priscilla Fontaine to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the December 2023 meeting.

Yuki Tanaka opened the board meeting and confirmed that the company had achieved $10M in annualised recurring revenue at the end of Q1 2024, representing 65% growth year-on-year.  CEO Samuel Osei presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 62%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 18 months at the current burn rate.  Yuki Tanaka noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q3 2025 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 5 new engineering roles and 3 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Diana Ostrowski, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in June 2024.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Yuki Tanaka to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the June 2024 meeting.

Yuki Tanaka opened the board meeting and confirmed that the company had achieved $18M in annualised recurring revenue at the end of Q3 2024, representing 85% growth year-on-year.  CEO Samuel Osei presented the business update, covering product roadmap, sales pipeline, customer retention, and headcount.

The board reviewed and approved the management accounts for the quarter.  Gross margin for the period was 66%, and the company maintained a cash runway of 24 months at the current burn rate.  Yuki Tanaka noted that the company is on track to reach profitability in Q1 2025 if growth targets are met.

The board approved a revised hiring plan, adding 9 new engineering roles and 5 sales roles in the following quarter.  The compensation committee, chaired by Diana Ostrowski, approved updated stock option grants for three senior hires joining in December 2024.

Action items for the next board meeting: management to provide a detailed competitive analysis, Yuki Tanaka to circulate revised financial model incorporating updated macro assumptions, and the CEO to present a three-year strategic plan by the December 2024 meeting.


------------------------------------------------------------

Chair:      Diana Ostrowski

==============================================================================
PART 13: VALUATION METHODOLOGY AND FAIR VALUE AUDIT TRAIL
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Valuation Policy Overview
------------------------------------------------------------

Meridian Capital Partners measures the fair value of all portfolio investments in accordance with ASC 820 (Fair Value Measurement) and IPEV Valuation Guidelines (December 2022 edition).  Valuations are prepared quarterly by the finance team under the supervision of Alejandro Torres and reviewed independently by the firm's external auditor, KPMG LLP.

All Level 3 fair value measurements (privately held equity and debt instruments without observable market prices) are reviewed by the Valuation Committee, which comprises Alejandro Torres (chair), Tomasz Kowalczyk, Helena Voss, and an independent valuation advisor from FTI Consulting.  The Valuation Committee meets within 30 days of each quarter-end.

Primary valuation methodologies applied are: (1) Revenue Multiple — applied to high-growth software and technology companies using a peer group of 8–12 publicly traded comparables; (2) EBITDA Multiple — applied to infrastructure and services businesses; (3) Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) — applied where long-dated contracted cash flows exist; (4) Cost Minus Impairment — applied to early-stage companies with limited trading history.

Where multiple methodologies are applied, the Valuation Committee exercises judgement in weighting the approaches, taking into account the stage, sector, and specific circumstances of each investment.  Material deviations from prior-quarter valuations require a written memorandum from the lead partner.

The Valuation Committee specifically reviewed the Level 3 inputs applied to DataForge, ZephyrData, and VaultChain in Q4 2024, given the deterioration in comparable company multiples and the balance-sheet stress identified in each company.  Downward adjustments were approved for all three companies following Tomasz Kowalczyk's risk review.


------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------
Revenue Multiple Peer Groups
------------------------------------------------------------

Enterprise SaaS Peer Group — Median Revenue Multiple: 8.5x
  Comparable companies: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, HubSpot, Zendesk, Veeva, Coupa, Sprinklr

FinTech Peer Group — Median Revenue Multiple: 11.2x
  Comparable companies: Adyen, Stripe (priv.), Wise, Marqeta, Brex, Checkout.com, Klarna (priv.), Nuvei

HealthTech Peer Group — Median Revenue Multiple: 7.8x
  Comparable companies: Doximity, Health Catalyst, Phreesia, Evolent, Accolade, Privia Health, SOC Telemed, GoodRx

CleanTech Peer Group — Median Revenue Multiple: 14.3x
  Comparable companies: Enphase, SolarEdge, Array Technologies, Shoals Technologies, Stem, Altus Power, Fluence Energy, Nextracker

PART 14: LEGAL AND COMPLIANCE REVIEW
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Legal and Regulatory Overview
------------------------------------------------------------

James Whitfield, General Counsel and Partner, oversees all legal and regulatory matters for Meridian Capital Partners and its managed funds.  Fatima Al-Rashid, Partner, provides additional regulatory expertise in MENA jurisdictions and Islamic finance structures.  The firm retains external legal counsel in all key jurisdictions including Linklaters (London), Latham & Watkins (New York), and Allen & Gledhill (Singapore).

Meridian Capital Partners (UK) LLP is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) under the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD).  The firm holds permissions for managing alternative investment funds (AIFs) and advising on investments.  The annual AIFMD transparency report for fiscal 2024 was filed by James Whitfield on March 31, 2025.

The EU-domiciled funds (Meridian Growth Fund IV SCSP and Meridian Infrastructure Fund II SCSP, both Luxembourg-domiciled) are subject to AIFMD as implemented in Luxembourg by the CSSF.  Fatima Al-Rashid coordinated with the Luxembourg-based AIFM, Meridian Management S.A., to ensure full AIFMD compliance.

Under SFDR, Meridian Climate Opportunities Fund I is classified as an Article 9 fund (dark green), and Meridian Growth Fund V will be classified as Article 8 upon launch.  Sophie Leclercq and James Whitfield jointly prepared the Principal Adverse Impact (PAI) statement and periodic reports for the Article 9 fund.

AML/KYC: All new LP investors undergo enhanced due diligence in accordance with the firm's AML/KYC policy, last updated in October 2024 to reflect the EU's 6th Anti-Money Laundering Directive (6AMLD).  Fatima Al-Rashid chairs the AML Committee, which reviews high-risk investor cases.  No suspicious activity reports were filed in fiscal 2024.

James Whitfield managed three LP side-letter requests during fiscal 2024, relating to ERISA compliance, MFN provisions, and transparency reporting obligations for a public pension fund investor.  All side-letter terms were reviewed by the Investment Committee and determined to be consistent with fund governance.

Litigation and Disputes
------------------------------------------------------------

As of March 31, 2025, Meridian Capital Partners is not a party to any material litigation.  James Whitfield confirmed that the minor contractual dispute with a former service provider, disclosed in the FY2023 Annual Report, was settled out of court in February 2024 for an amount that was not material to the firm.

Fatima Al-Rashid disclosed a regulatory inquiry from the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) relating to marketing activities in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC).  The inquiry is at an early stage and James Whitfield has engaged local counsel Clifford Chance LLP to respond.  The firm does not currently hold a DFSA licence and the inquiry relates to whether certain LP communications constituted a marketing communication under DIFC rules.

==============================================================================
APPENDIX B: GLOSSARY OF TERMS
==============================================================================

AUM
    Assets Under Management — the total market value of investments managed by a fund on behalf of its limited partners.

IRR
    Internal Rate of Return — the annualised rate of return on an investment, accounting for the timing of cash flows.

MOIC
    Multiple on Invested Capital — the ratio of total value (realised and unrealised) to the total capital invested.

DPI
    Distributed to Paid-In — the ratio of capital returned to limited partners to the total capital called from them.

RVPI
    Residual Value to Paid-In — the ratio of the current fair value of unrealised investments to total capital called.

TVPI
    Total Value to Paid-In — the sum of DPI and RVPI, representing total value created relative to capital invested.

LP
    Limited Partner — an investor in a private equity fund who provides capital but does not participate in day-to-day management.

GP
    General Partner — the fund manager who makes investment decisions and manages the fund on behalf of limited partners.

Carry / Carried Interest
    The share of profits (typically 20%) that the General Partner receives once limited partners have received their invested capital plus a preferred return.

Hurdle Rate
    The minimum rate of return (typically 8%) that a fund must achieve before the General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest.

Clawback
    A provision requiring the General Partner to return carried interest previously received if the fund ultimately underperforms the hurdle rate on a cumulative basis.

NAV
    Net Asset Value — the fair value of all assets in a fund, net of liabilities, at a given point in time.

PIK
    Payment in Kind — interest or dividends paid in additional securities rather than cash.

Vintage Year
    The year in which a fund makes its first capital call or closes on its first investment.

Dry Powder
    Committed but uncalled capital available for future investments.

Co-Investment
    An investment made by a limited partner alongside the fund in a specific portfolio company, typically on more favourable terms.

Secondary
    The purchase or sale of existing private equity fund interests or portfolio company stakes in the secondary market.

SFDR
    Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation — EU regulation requiring financial market participants to disclose how sustainability risks are integrated into investment decisions.

UNPRI
    United Nations Principles for Responsible Investment — a voluntary framework for incorporating ESG factors into investment analysis and decision-making.

ESG
    Environmental, Social, and Governance — a framework for assessing the sustainability and ethical impact of an investment or business.

Cap Table
    Capitalisation Table — a spreadsheet or document showing the equity ownership structure of a company, including all shareholders and option holders.

Pre-Money Valuation
    The valuation of a company before a new round of funding is added, used to calculate the price per share for the new investors.

Post-Money Valuation
    The valuation of a company after new capital has been invested, equal to the pre-money valuation plus the new investment.

Anti-Dilution
    A provision protecting existing investors from dilution in future financing rounds that value the company lower than the current round.

Liquidation Preference
    A clause specifying the order and amount in which investors are paid in the event of a liquidation, sale, or IPO.

Tag-Along
    A contractual right allowing minority shareholders to join a transaction if majority shareholders sell their stake.

Drag-Along
    A right allowing majority shareholders to force minority shareholders to join in the sale of the company.

EBITDA
    Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation — a measure of a company's core operating profitability.

ARR
    Annual Recurring Revenue — the value of the recurring revenue components of a subscription business, normalised to a one-year period.

NRR
    Net Revenue Retention — a metric measuring revenue expansion from existing customers, accounting for churn, contraction, and expansion.

------------------------------------------------------------
Fee Calculations — Illustrative Example
------------------------------------------------------------

The following example illustrates the management fee and carried interest calculation for Meridian Growth Fund V, assuming a $1.2B close and a fund return of 2.3x MOIC (net of fees and carry).

  Management Fee (investment period, on committed capital):
    $1,200M × 1.75% = $21.0M per annum
    Over 5-year investment period: $105.0M total management fees

  Management Fee (post-investment period, on invested capital):
    $1,020M (est. invested) × 1.0% = $10.2M per annum
    Over 5-year harvest period: $51.0M additional management fees

  Carried Interest (assuming 2.3x MOIC):
    Gross proceeds: $2,760M
    Return of capital: $1,200M
    Preferred return (8% × 10 years): $1,200M × [(1.08)^10 - 1] ≈ $1,389M cumulative
    Profits above hurdle: $2,760M - $1,200M - $589M preferred return = $971M
    Carried interest (20%): $194.2M to General Partner
    Net to LPs: $2,565.8M (after carry) = net MOIC of 2.14x on committed capital

APPENDIX D: CO-INVESTMENT LOG
==============================================================================


------------------------------------------------------------
Co-Investment Programme Overview
------------------------------------------------------------

Meridian Capital Partners operates a co-investment programme under which certain qualifying limited partners may invest alongside the fund in specific portfolio companies, typically at a reduced or nil management fee and carry.  Co-investment rights are allocated on the basis of fund commitment size and prior co-investment participation.

Robert Ashworth and Alejandro Torres oversee the co-investment programme.  James Whitfield maintains the co-investment register and ensures compliance with each fund's constitutional documents.  During fiscal 2024, the firm offered co-investment rights on five transactions totalling $340M, of which $280M was taken up by qualifying LPs.

Co-investors are required to execute a Co-Investment Agreement and a side letter with each fund prior to closing their co-investment.  Fatima Al-Rashid reviews co-investment documentation for MENA-based LPs to ensure compliance with local regulatory requirements.

------------------------------------------------------------
Co-Investment Rights Allocation Policy
------------------------------------------------------------

Co-investment rights are offered to LPs in the following priority order:

  Tier 1 (≥$100M commitment): Right to participate in all co-investments up to 15% of the total deal size.
  Tier 2 ($50M–$99M commitment): Right to participate in co-investments up to 10% of the total deal size.
  Tier 3 ($25M–$49M commitment): Right to participate in co-investments up to 5% of the total deal size on a first-come, first-served basis.
  Tier 4 (<$25M commitment): Co-investment offered on a best-efforts basis subject to availability.

Alejandro Torres distributes co-investment opportunity notices within 48 hours of Investment Committee approval of the primary transaction.  LPs have a 72-hour response window.  Unused allocation is first redistributed to other Tier 1 LPs and then down the tier structure.

Robert Ashworth presented the co-investment programme review to the LP Advisory Committee on October 14, 2024.  The committee expressed strong support for the programme and requested that the minimum response window be extended to five business days for future co-investment opportunities, effective Q1 2025.  James Whitfield is updating the co-investment side letter template accordingly.
